You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily｜Trump Claims U.S. Navy Has 100% Control of the Strait of Hormuz; Oil Surges on Inflation Concerns; U.S. Stocks Edge Lower with Tech Under Pressure (August 11, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Developments
Markets Focus on This Week’s Inflation Data; Rate-Hike Expectations Still Shaped by Jobs and Oil
After the July non-farm payrolls came in far weaker than expected, markets have significantly reduced near-term rate-hike probabilities.
This week’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) releases will be the key pricing catalysts for the next policy path.
The sharp rise in oil prices driven by the Hormuz standoff may rekindle inflation expectations.
Market Impact : Weaker employment and rising oil prices create a tug-of-war. The near-term Fed path remains uncertain, and market sensitivity to incoming data is elevated.
International Commodities
Trump Claims U.S. Navy Has 100% Control of the Strait of Hormuz; Oil Rises Sharply
Trump stated that the only force currently controlling the Strait of Hormuz is the U.S. Navy, describing the blockade as “infallible” and a “steel wall.” He said the entire waterway has been mine-swept, is open to non-Iranian vessels, but does not allow entry into Iranian ports.
Trump also demanded that Iran compensate for casualties and losses related to the conflict, adding a new variable to reopening negotiations.
Iran reiterated its conditions for reopening and said an agreement with Oman on new shipping lanes is nearing completion.
Market Impact : Uncertainty over actual navigation through the strait persists. Oil rebounded sharply, reintroducing inflation and geopolitical risk premia and heightening near-term volatility in energy markets.
U.S. Equity Macro
U.S. Stocks Pull Back on Monday; Tech and Energy Diverge
The three major U.S. indexes closed modestly lower amid inflation concerns triggered by the oil rally .
Intel announced it may sell $15 billion of stock to support AI and manufacturing activities, pressuring its shares.
Names such as Berkshire that beat earnings expectations held up relatively well.
Market Impact : Geopolitics and inflation expectations dominated sen time nt. Capital rotated between energy and tech, and the overall market tone remained cautious.
II. Market Recap
Commodities & FX Performance
Spot Gold : ~$4,414/oz, +0.6%
Spot Silver : ~$65/oz, +0.2%
WTI Crude : ~$82.2/bbl, +0.07%
Brent Crude : ~$83.98/bbl, +0.12%
U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) : ~99.75, -0.06%
Driver Analysis : Trump’s claim that the U.S. Navy has 100% control of the Strait of Hormuz and is maintaining the blockade, combined with disagreements over compensation, left the reopening outlook unclear and pushed crude higher. Gold traded cautiously amid the interplay between a firmer dollar and safe-haven demand. The asset linkage is clear: geopolitical stalemate → higher oil → rising inflation expectations → dollar support, while risk assets faced pressure. Near-term commodity moves will remain highly dependent on actual navigation progress through the strait and this week’s inflation data.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$64,037, -1.55%
ETH : ~$1,874, +2.12%
Total Crypto Market Cap : ~$2.27 trillion, -0.4%
Liquidations (24h) : Total ~$205 million, of which shorts ~$59.25 million
Bitget BTC/ USDT Liquidation Map : BTC currently around $63,950. Dense long liquidations are concentrated near $63,300–$63,700; a break below $63,500 could trigger cascading long stop-outs. Short-liquidation pressure is notable at $64,300–$65,000; a breakout above $64,400 could further force short covering. Short-term volatility risk remains elevated.
Spot ETF Flows : BTC spot ETFs recorded a dynamic net outflow of approximately $91 million over the past 24 hours.
Driver Analysis : The sharp rise in oil and heightened geopolitical uncertainty tempered risk appetite, leaving the crypto market in a high-level consolidation. BTC held above the $64,500 area earlier but slipped, while ETH showed relative resilience. ETF flows turned to a modest net outflow, and liquidation volumes remained manageable. On the macro side, weaker employment and higher oil prices are offsetting each other. Near-term crypto price action is likely to remain range-bound; attention turns to this week’s inflation data and its impact on liquidity expectations.
U.S. Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at ~53,976 (-0.1%), modest pullback
S&P 500 : Closed at ~7,753 (-0.1%), retreated from record highs
Nasdaq : Closed at ~26,605 (-0.3%), tech under pressure
Tech Giants Performance
NVDA : ~$217.55 (-2.86%)
AAPL : ~$308.26 (-1.62%)
MSFT : ~$506.06 (+1.21%)
GOOGL : ~$357.52 (+0.91%)
AMZN : ~$278.09 (+1.32%)
META : ~$594.92 (+0.48%)
TSLA : ~$330.88 (+0.70%)
[...]
Performance Summary & Driver Analysis : U.S. equities edged lower on Monday, with the Nasdaq posting the largest decline. Nvidia and Apple came under clear pressure, while Microsoft , Amazon , Google, Meta and Tesla advanced, underscoring continued divergence within tech. The sharp oil rally reignited inflation concerns and partially offset the rate-cut expectations that had followed the weak jobs data. Markets are balancing geopolitical risk against macro data, with capital favoring cloud and software names that offer higher earnings visibility.
[...]
Representative stocks: Nvidia (-2.86%), related chip names broadly lower
[...]
Representative stocks: Microsoft (+1.21%), Amazon (+1.32%) relatively resilient
[...]
Drivers: Amid rising geopolitical and inflation uncertainty, capital preferred names with already-delivered revenue and clear commercialization paths. Sustained high growth at Azure and AWS gave cloud giants relative defensive characteristics, creating a clear divergence from high-volatility, high-valuation hardware stocks.
[...]
1. Nvidia (NVDA) – Falls Nearly 3%, Semiconductors Under Pressure
[...]
Event Overview : Nvidia shares fell approximately 2.86% to $217.55, ranking among the weaker large-cap tech names. Markets grew concerned that the Hormuz standoff-driven oil rally could rekindle inflation expectations and thereby affect subsequent liquidity and the Fed’s policy path. Market Interpretation : The earlier weaker-than-expected non-farm data had lifted risk appetite and allowed AI-hardware sentiment to recover. The sharp rise in oil rapidly altered the macro narrative, prompting capital to reassess the rate path and valuation pressure. As a high-valuation, high-elasticity compute leader, Nvidia typically comes under pressure first when inflation worries intensify. The long-term AI compute demand thesis remains intact, but near-term price action is highly sensitive to macro liquidity and rate expectations; profit-taking and position adjustments acted in combination. Investment Implication : Watch this week’s CPI and PPI data for their impact on inflation expectations, as well as whether large-customer capital-expenditure guidance continues to support the demand narrative. Volatility may increase around the data releases.
[...]
2. Apple (AAPL) – Falls More Than 1.6%, Relative Laggard
[...]
Event Overview : Apple shares declined approximately 1.62% to $308.26, underperforming most large-cap tech peers and extending its recent relative lag. Market Interpretation : In phases of converging risk appetite when capital prefers cloud and software names, consumer-electronics and hardware companies typically show limited elasticity. Although Apple possesses robust cash flow and a services moat, the market is currently more focused on marginal changes in hardware demand and the actual pull of AI features on the upgrade cycle. Relative to companies already delivering cloud-revenue growth, Apple is receiving less capital preference in the current macro environment. Investment Implication : Continued monitoring of the product cycle, the sustainability of services growth, and the tangible impact of Apple Intelligence and other AI features on user upgrade willingness is required.
[...]
4. Amazon (AMZN) – Gains More Than 1.3%, Following the Cloud Logic
[...]
5. Tesla (TSLA) – Modest Gain
